d: An overview of all animation tools in Roblox Studio.
h:
Animation is the process of applying motion to your characters, objects, and environments to create an engaging and dynamic game. While there are many ways to make objects move and interact, animation in Roblox typically refers to customizing an expressive movement of a specific character or group of parts.

Animation can apply to any Roblox part or group of parts. Different types of objects can utilize various animation features. The following are the general categories of animatable objects:

  • Simple objects, such as a basic part, can only animate changes across the part's single position or rotation property.
  • Rigs, or parts connected by joints like AnimationConstraints or Bones, can articulate positional and rotational movement between their joints, like elbows and wrists. Rigged models can take advantage of animation features like inverse kinematics to quickly and programmatically apply movement in response to environments and events.
  • Standard and advanced R15 rigs can use animations from Roblox's character animation library and other movement features, regardless of if it's a player or non-player character model.

Animation Editor

The Animation Editor allows you to design and publish custom animations on rigs. You can move the joints that connect individual sections of a rig to create poses, and the editor smoothly animates the rig from pose-to-pose.

Inverse kinematics

You can use inverse kinematics APIs to automatically create animations and poses based on environmental and external events. With inverse kinematics, you can procedurally generate various animation events, such as having a character's head track a bird flying in the sky, or making a character's arm automatically reach for a door knob when nearby.

Animation events

An animation event is a specific point in an animation that triggers an action. You can define animation event markers across the Animation Editor timeline span, then use AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal() to detect those markers as the animation runs to perform specific actions, such as playing a sound effect whenever the user's foot touches the ground.

kid.simple: Animation means making things move in an expressive way, like a character waving, dancing, or swinging a sword. This page is a quick map of Roblox's animation tools. It explains which objects can be animated, and points you to the Animation Editor, inverse kinematics, and animation events. Start here to figure out which tool fits what you want to make.
kid.analogy: A rig is like an action figure with bendable joints. Animating it is like moving its arms and legs a little at a time for a stop-motion movie.
keyPoints: Simple objects, like a single part, can only animate their position or rotation.
Rigs are groups of parts connected by joints (like `AnimationConstraint` or `Bone`), so they can bend at elbows, wrists, and other joints.
Standard and advanced R15 rigs can use Roblox's character animation library, whether they are players or non-player characters.
The Animation Editor lets you pose a rig at different times and smoothly animates between the poses.
Inverse kinematics can make poses automatically, like a head following a flying bird or a hand reaching for a door knob.
Animation events are markers on the timeline. A script can detect them with `AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal()`, for example to play a footstep sound.

terms.animation: Planned movement for characters or objects, like a run cycle or a wave.
terms.rig: A model whose parts are linked by joints so they can move like a body.
terms.joint: The connection between two parts of a rig, like a shoulder or knee, where movement happens.
terms.R15: Roblox's standard character body made of 15 parts, such as upper arm, lower arm, and hand.
terms.inverse kinematics: Telling the hand or foot where to go, and letting Roblox figure out how the elbow and shoulder should bend to get there.
terms.procedurally: Made by code while the game runs, instead of drawn ahead of time by hand.
terms.animation event: A named marker at a moment in an animation, like at 0.5 seconds, that scripts can react to.
terms.articulate: Bend or move at a joint.

watchOut: Trying to make a bending animation on a single part. Only rigs with joints can bend; simple parts just move or turn.
Mixing up the tools. Use the Animation Editor for hand-made motions, inverse kinematics for motions that react to the world, and events to trigger code during an animation.
